issues.legal_issue: A substantial increase in property value during litigation does not, by itself, justify denying specific performance to a purchaser who was not in breach.
material_facts: The purchaser filed suit within a month of the agreed possession date and had already paid more than half of the purchase price.
The courts had found that the purchaser was always ready and willing to perform and that the sellers breached the agreement.

The purchaser had continued to pursue her claim while other purchasers settled, and was willing to accept the incomplete flat without a price reduction or holding the sellers responsible for its incomplete state.
The property’s value had increased substantially during the prolonged litigation.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was entitled to specific performance notwithstanding the increase in property value; that increase alone was not a reason to deny relief or deprive her of its benefit. The decree was conditional on payment of an additional reasonable amount.
issues.legal_principle: Specific performance is discretionary and need not be granted merely because it is legally available. A court may consider a phenomenal increase in value among the circumstances relevant to its decision, but ordinarily should not deny specific performance on that ground alone. It must assess the totality of circumstances, including which party defaulted, whether either party seeks an undue advantage, and the hardship to the defendant. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this principle; it refers to the differing opinions of the two judges who heard the appeal earlier in the same matter.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and purchaser_not_in_breach and seller_breached_agreement and (purchaser_sued_promptly or purchaser_paid_more_than_half or purchaser_willing_to_accept_incomplete_property) and property_value_increased_during_litigation

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.purchaser_not_in_breach: The purchaser was found ready and willing to perform and had not breached the agreement.
predicates.seller_breached_agreement: The seller failed to carry out the agreement.
predicates.purchaser_sued_promptly: The purchaser filed suit soon after the agreed time for performance passed.
predicates.purchaser_paid_more_than_half: The purchaser had paid more than half of the agreed purchase price.
predicates.purchaser_willing_to_accept_incomplete_p: The purchaser agreed to accept the property in its incomplete condition without a price reduction or holding the seller responsible for the incompleteness.
predicates.property_value_increased_during_litigati: The property’s value increased while the litigation was pending.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking specific performance was not in breach and the seller breached, an increase in property value during litigation does not by itself defeat the purchaser’s claim, particularly where the purchaser sued promptly, paid a substantial part of the price, or accepted the property incomplete.

issues.legal_issue: A court granting specific performance may require a purchaser to pay a reasonable additional amount, assessed in light of the parties’ conduct and the circumstances of the case.
material_facts: The sellers had been deprived for many years of the unpaid balance of the purchase price.
The purchaser was willing to pay interest on that unpaid balance and to accept the incomplete flat without seeking a reduction in the agreed price.
The sellers had breached the agreement, and the purchaser had not defaulted.
The purchaser had continued the litigation for more than three decades.
The court considered a payment of Rs.40,00,000 too onerous, but considered it reasonable to require an additional payment of Rs.6,25,000 instead of the original unpaid balance of Rs.25,000.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser could obtain specific performance on condition that she pay the sellers Rs.6,25,000 in addition to the amount already paid, within six weeks; failure to comply would extinguish her entitlement to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: The court’s equitable discretion in granting or refusing specific performance includes the power to impose a reasonable condition, including an additional payment. The amount and whether such a condition is appropriate depend on the totality of the circumstances, including who defaulted, whether a party is seeking an undue advantage, and the hardship the order would cause. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this principle; it notes the differing opinions of the two judges who heard the appeal earlier in the same matter.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and purchaser_not_in_breach and seller_breached_agreement and seller_deprived_of_unpaid_price_for_years and (purchaser_willing_to_accept_incomplete_property or large_additional_payment_would_be_onerous)

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.purchaser_not_in_breach: The purchaser was found ready and willing to perform and had not breached the agreement.
predicates.seller_breached_agreement: The seller failed to carry out the agreement.
predicates.seller_deprived_of_unpaid_price_for_year: The seller remained without the unpaid part of the purchase price for a prolonged period.
predicates.purchaser_willing_to_accept_incomplete_p: The purchaser agreed to accept the property in its incomplete condition without a price reduction or holding the seller responsible for the incompleteness.
predicates.large_additional_payment_would_be_onerou: The court found that the proposed large additional payment would impose an excessive burden on the purchaser.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking specific performance has not defaulted, the seller has breached and been deprived of the unpaid price for a prolonged period, and the purchaser accepts the property incomplete or a large additional payment would be onerous, the court may require a reasonable additional payment as a condition of specific performance.
